title: Auterion Skynode S and Auterion Visual Navigation
summary: Auterion sells PX4-derived AuterionOS plus Skynode flight/mission computers. Skynode S (2024) is a small integrated autopilot/mission computer marketed for operation when GNSS and links are jammed; Auterion Visual Navigation is the company's camera-based position source, named in its 2025 DIU Artemis completion announcement.
key_takeaways: Vendor claim: AuterionOS detects GNSS jamming/spoofing and stops trusting GNSS (Jan 2024 announcement)
Vendor/press claim: used in Ukraine; no public accuracy figures found
Open-source base is PX4; the visual navigation layer is proprietary

title: Shield AI Hivemind autonomy stack
summary: Hivemind is Shield AI's onboard autonomy software, flown on its V-BAT and on partner aircraft. In an interview the CTO describes a state-estimation framework fusing visual, EO/IR and inertial observations so the aircraft keeps operating without GNSS or comms.
key_takeaways: Vendor description: multi-sensor state estimation for GNSS-denied and comms-denied flight
No published accuracy numbers found
ViDAR (acquired with Sentient Vision, 2024) is an EO/IR detection product, not a navigation source

title: Helsing HX-2 - map/landmark-based GNSS-denied navigation (navigation aspect only)
summary: Helsing's HX-2 is a loitering UAS supplied to Ukraine. Indexed here only for its navigation approach: press reporting says an onboard computer with stored map data lets it navigate by recognising landmarks when satellite navigation is denied. Helsing navigation job postings mention vision-aided, terrain-relative, celestial and signals-of-opportunity methods.
key_takeaways: Press/vendor claim: landmark recognition against stored maps; no public accuracy data
Shows the European market expects map-based visual nav as a baseline feature

title: Q-CTRL Ironstone Opal quantum-assured magnetic navigation
summary: Q-CTRL's navigation product pairs quantum magnetometers with its software to match measured crustal magnetic anomalies against maps (MagNav). The company reports flight, ground and maritime trials and positions it as a GNSS backup for aviation, including work with Airbus.
key_takeaways: Vendor claims (not independent): RNP 0.3 met in flight (error under 0.3 nm for 95% of a flight); the linked case study claims 50x lower positioning uncertainty than an INS over a ~500 km flight and at least 11x with the sensor inside the cabin; other Q-CTRL materials give different multipliers
Vendor claim: RTCA DO-160 environmental qualification - not an airworthiness or RNP operational approval
Underlying method is the same map-matching problem as the open AFRL/MIT MagNav challenge

title: SandboxAQ AQNav geomagnetic navigation
summary: AQNav is SandboxAQ's magnetic anomaly navigation system: magnetometers plus learned compensation, matched against magnetic anomaly maps. Flight-tested with Acubed (Airbus) on a Beechcraft Baron using public maps, and, per later SandboxAQ announcements, with the USAF on C-17/C-130J and in 2026 on a Northrop Grumman Lumberjack drone.
key_takeaways: Vendor claims (July 2025 Acubed campaign, 150+ flight hours on a Beechcraft Baron 58 with the public NAMAM map): within RNP 2 100% of the time and RNP 1 95%; outperformed INS without GNSS on every flight over 2 h
Sept 2026 drone test announcement gave no error figures (noted by press)
Accepted into the 2025 NATO DIANA cohort (vendor/press)

title: Xona Space Systems Pulsar LEO PNT constellation
summary: Xona is building Pulsar, a commercial LEO constellation broadcasting dedicated L-band navigation signals with authentication. Pulsar-0 launched in June/July 2025 as an in-orbit demonstrator; production satellites and initial service were planned for 2026-2027 per later reporting, and the FCC granted conditional approval in August 2026 (initially 16 satellites, more after a debris review).
key_takeaways: LEO PNT signals are stronger at the ground than MEO GNSS, which is the anti-jam argument
Service is not yet generally available; dates in press reports conflict
Open work in this space uses existing LEO signals of opportunity (Starlink, Iridium Doppler) instead

title: TrustPoint - C-band LEO PNT
summary: TrustPoint is developing a commercial C-band LEO navigation constellation. Its third demonstration satellite (Time Flies) launched in June 2025 carrying a C-band payload for testing partner receivers.
key_takeaways: Vendor claim: commercial GPS alternative from LEO; no independent performance reports found
C-band choice moves PNT away from crowded and jammed L-band

title: Iridium PNT (Satellite Time and Location) and Iridium PNT ASIC
summary: Iridium broadcasts a high-power LEO timing and location signal (STL, from the Satelles acquisition) usable as a GNSS backup and cross-check. A dedicated PNT ASIC was unveiled in October 2025 and announced commercially available in July 2026; integrators include Solace and Skyband, and VectorNav/NAL Research announced STL-aided INS work in 2025.
key_takeaways: Positioning is coarse compared to GNSS; main value is timing and an independent plausibility check
Vendor claim on ASIC size: 8 x 8 mm, under 0.2 g (Iridium fact sheet, Oct 2025)
Open LEO Doppler code in the index can use Iridium signals of opportunity without a subscription

title: Honeywell Vision Aided Navigation (Alternative Navigation Suite)
summary: Honeywell's VAN correlates live visible or IR imagery against onboard reference maps for an absolute fix, paired with its inertial units. It sits in an Alternative Navigation Suite with magnetic-anomaly and celestial modules.
key_takeaways: Vendor description: passive, sensor-agnostic image-to-map correlation
Press claim: 'GPS-like' performance on Embraer E170 and AW139 tests; no numbers published
Same problem as open UAV absolute visual localization benchmarks

title: Honeywell HGuide o480 single-card INS and HGuide i700 IMU
summary: HGuide o480 (May 2025) is a single-card INS for small UAVs and ground robots that accepts velocity aiding (e.g. Honeywell radar velocity sensor) and embeds a Septentrio receiver with AIM+ anti-jam/anti-spoof. The HGuide i700 IMU is marketed as near navigation grade with a no-license-required export classification.
key_takeaways: Shows the commodity pattern: tactical IMU + velocity aid + hardened GNSS in one card
Export classification is a selling point, which matters for team hardware choices

title: Advanced Navigation Boreas FOG INS with LVS laser velocity sensor
summary: Advanced Navigation's Boreas fibre-optic-gyro INS line, fused with its LVS laser velocity sensor or wheel odometry, is marketed for long GNSS-denied ground and maritime runs; reported trials include a US Army testbed and an underground mine.
key_takeaways: Vendor/press claims: 11.7 m error over 65 km with GNSS jammed (wheel-encoder config, US Army testbed, linked article); better than 0.1% of distance travelled in BHP's Callio mine trial (Advanced Navigation case study)
Strategy is inertial-centric dead reckoning with velocity aiding, not vision

title: Inertial Labs VINS visual-aided INS (with Maxar Raptor)
summary: Launched June 2025, VINS combines an Inertial Labs INS with Maxar Raptor software that matches camera frames to Maxar Precision3D satellite-derived 3D maps for absolute position on long-range UAV flights.
key_takeaways: Vendor claims: about 35 m horizontal / 5 m vertical without GNSS
Options for Iridium-based PNT and M-code receivers
Commercial map product (Precision3D) is the moat; open teams use free orthophotos and DEMs

title: Safran VersaPNT and Geonyx resilient PNT units
summary: Safran's defense PNT range includes VersaPNT (GNSS receiver + IMU + disciplined oscillator with jamming/spoofing detection and NTP/PTP time serving) and the Geonyx HRG-based INS; GPS World reports a NAVKITE kit combining Geonyx M with VersaSync for French Navy commandos.
key_takeaways: Combined position + timing holdover in one box is the standard defense product shape
Detection flags and holdover timing are reproducible in open stacks at lower grade

title: SBG Systems Ellipse INS - 2025 GNSS-denied firmware
summary: A March 2025 free firmware update for SBG's Ellipse (v3 hardware) adds jamming/spoofing detection flags and lets users reject or re-enable GNSS and other aiding sensors without resetting the filter.
key_takeaways: Vendor claim: improved accuracy in GNSS-denied and magnetically disturbed conditions
Integrity flags plus manual sensor rejection is now an expected feature even in small INS

title: VectorNav - Iridium STL-aided INS collaboration with NAL Research
summary: VectorNav makes small tactical-grade IMU/GNSS-INS units widely used on research drones (PX4 has a driver). In April 2025 it announced work with NAL Research on Iridium STL-aided INS for GNSS-denied operation.
key_takeaways: Collaboration announcement, not a shipped product feature
VN-series units are a common drop-in for PX4 testbeds

title: Spirent GSS7000 and PNT X GNSS/PNT simulators
summary: Spirent's lab simulators generate multi-GNSS RF with controllable interference and spoofing (meaconing, trajectory spoofing, nav data spoofing) for hardware-in-the-loop receiver testing; PNT X extends this to combined PNT/sensor simulation.
key_takeaways: Lab-grade, export-controlled tooling; judges from industry will know it
Open alternatives are SDR-based signal simulators - legal only into a cable or shielded enclosure

title: Safran Skydel simulation engine / GSG-8 GNSS simulator (ex-Orolia)
summary: Skydel is the SDR/GPU-based simulation engine behind Safran's GSG-8 simulators, with built-in jamming and spoofing scenarios, CRPA wavefront variants and LEO PNT signal options; Safran offers it to universities through an academic programme.
key_takeaways: Vendor datasheet: jamming and spoofing generated without extra hardware
Spoofing workflows run a 'truth' and a 'spoofer' instance - a useful mental model for test design

title: infiniDome GPSdome / GPSdome 2 small-UAS anti-jam module
summary: infiniDome sells retrofit anti-jam modules that sit between antenna elements and a commercial GNSS receiver on small drones and vehicles; GPSdome 2 is dual-band with up to four elements for nulling several jammer directions.
key_takeaways: Vendor claim: CRPA-like protection without CRPA cost or export restrictions
Weight figures differ across press releases (500 g in the linked GPS World piece, 350 g elsewhere)

title: Twist Robotics OSCAR visual navigation module (Ukraine)
summary: Ukrainian company Twist Robotics announced OSCAR in January 2026: a camera-based module that recognises landmarks, matches them to a map and feeds coordinates to the UAV autopilot when GNSS is jammed.
key_takeaways: Vendor claim: platforms with the module have flown more than 500,000 km
Architecture (camera => map match => coordinates into autopilot) is the same one open repos implement

title: Blue Arrow - Ukrainian visual navigation for drones (Brave1 cluster)
summary: Brave1 cluster member Blue Arrow was presented by Ukraine's minister Fedorov in 2025 as having an autonomous visual navigation system that lets drones fly without GNSS under jamming and spoofing.
key_takeaways: Claim relayed from a ministerial post; no technical detail or numbers published
One of many Ukrainian vendors in this niche (others named by Brave1: Norda Dynamics, The Fourth Law, ZIR)

title: Theseus Visual Navigation System (YC launch)
summary: US startup whose founders started at the February 2024 El Segundo Defense Tech Hackathon (Aviation Week coverage). Its VNS uses a camera, an IMU and pre-loaded satellite imagery to estimate position and feeds the drone a substitute GPS signal.
key_takeaways: Vendor claims: six months from hackathon to a SOCOM sale (YC launch post); integration under 30 minutes (company statement relayed by press)
Direct precedent that a hackathon visual-nav demo can become a product - and that judges have seen this pitch

title: Spleenlab VISIONAIRY perception and GNSS-free navigation software
summary: German company Spleenlab sells VISIONAIRY, an AI perception suite for drones (vendor description: VIO, map-based relocalization, EO/IR and LiDAR SLAM) that joined the Auterion ecosystem in 2022 and integrates with PX4/Auterion and ROS. Quantum Systems later acquired Spleenlab and uses it for GNSS-denied navigation (press).
key_takeaways: Vendor description only; no published accuracy
Module list mirrors what open VIO + VPR repos offer

title: UAVOS NavAI vision-based navigation module
summary: UAVOS markets NavAI as an add-on vision-based navigation module for UAS in GNSS-degraded conditions (GPS World product announcement).
key_takeaways: Product announcement; performance figures not verified here

title: DARPA Robust Quantum Sensors (RoQS) - Phase 1
summary: RoQS (solicitation DARPA-PS-25-11) aims to make quantum sensors robust to platform vibration and motion so they work on real vehicles; Phase 1 launched August 2025 with compact sensors to be tested on a government helicopter plus platform integration studies.
key_takeaways: Problem statement: quantum sensors lose their advantage on moving platforms
Signals where defense money is going for GNSS-independent inertial/magnetic sensing

title: DIU Transition of Quantum Sensing (TQS)
summary: DIU programme fielding quantum sensors for PNT: lines of effort cover quantum inertial sensors, gravimeters for gravity-aided naval navigation, quantum magnetic sensing, magnetic navigation and component insertion, with more than 10 field tests planned in the first ~12 months (announced March 2025).
key_takeaways: 18 named performers including Honeywell, Lockheed Martin, Q-CTRL, AOSense, Anduril, Northrop Grumman, Vector Atomic
Honeywell flew a quantum MagNav test on an Embraer 170 under TQS (press)

title: DAF-MIT AI Accelerator MagNav real-time C-17 demonstration (2023)
summary: In May 2023 the Air Force and MIT flew a real-time MagNav demo on a C-17A during exercise Golden Phoenix, training the compensation network in flight on a laptop. Follows the open MagNav challenge problem and dataset.
key_takeaways: No accuracy figure is public: the linked article and the official releases defer it to a government technical report. The value shown is RF independence
Public dataset and Julia/Python code make this the most reproducible alt-PNT track for a hackathon

title: UK quantum navigation flight trials (Infleqtion, BAE Systems, QinetiQ)
summary: In May 2024 an optical atomic clock and a cold-atom sensor flew on QinetiQ's RJ100 testbed from Boscombe Down, toward a quantum inertial navigation system concept. Linked to the UK National Quantum Strategy mission of quantum navigation on aircraft by 2030.
key_takeaways: Government claim: first publicly acknowledged in-flight tests of this kind
Government funding stated as nearly GBP 8 million

title: UK DASA Early Market Engagement: PNT problem statement for uncrewed systems
summary: Published September 2024. Asks for assured PNT for small UAS: low-cost, low-SWaP CRPA (multi-frequency, SDR-based), SDR/GPU GNSS receivers, AI for spoofing detection and multi-source fusion, as plug-in replacements for COTS GNSS.
key_takeaways: Explicit platform example: under 1.5 m wingspan
Unit cost must suit mass use - cost is a first-class requirement

title: UK national eLoran, Timing Centre and GNSS warning investment (2025)
summary: November 2025 UK announcement of about GBP 155M for a national timing centre, a sovereign eLoran system and GNSS interference warning; a Find a Tender notice targets eLoran IOC by 2028 and FOC by 2030.
key_takeaways: Terrestrial backup and GNSS warning, not only alt-nav on the vehicle

title: ESA NAVISP (Navigation Innovation and Support Programme)
summary: ESA's PNT R&D programme funding industry projects including GNSS-independent PNT; 2025 examples include ALL.SPACE (EUR 950k per the October 2025 ALL.SPACE announcement, signals of opportunity from a multi-orbit terminal, with GMV NSL) and maritime alt-PNT via VDES and R-Mode.
key_takeaways: Permanent open call route for European companies
Shows European emphasis on SoOP and terrestrial backups

title: European Defence Fund 2025 calls
summary: EDF 2025 work programme (EUR 1.065B) closed 16 October 2025 with 410 proposals; results expected April 2026. Indexed as the current EDF cycle; the explicit drone-navigation challenge topic in the index is from EDF 2024.
key_takeaways: No 2025 topic explicitly on GNSS-denied navigation confirmed in this pass
EDF 2024 challenge (multi-sensor drone navigation) is the best-matched prior topic

title: UNITE - Brave NATO: Brave1 and NATO Innovation HQ joint competition (2026)
summary: March 2026 programme pairing Ukrainian and NATO-country companies on joint solutions: first round EUR 10M, up to EUR 1M per project split between partners. Focus areas are counter-UAS and navigation where EW disrupts positioning; NATO-side funding limited to non-lethal categories.
key_takeaways: Ministerial framing: 'robust navigation in GPS-denied environments' as a critical field

title: EUDIS Defence Hackathon, 5th edition (Oct 2026) - GNSS-denied navigation challenge
summary: EU-funded 48-hour hackathon held 15-17 October 2026 at eight sites under the theme 'Autonomy on the Battlefield'. Common challenges were GNSS-denied navigation and swarm coordination, plus one local challenge per host (e.g. counter-UAS in Cyprus).
key_takeaways: Most direct precedent for this hackathon's likely problem statement
Eligibility: EU, Norway, Ukraine citizens aged 18+

title: European Defense Tech Hackathon series (Paris, London, Sheffield, Prague...)
summary: Independent recurring European defense hackathon series. The December 2024 Paris edition had a second-place magnetic navigation entry for underwater drones; 2025 London and Sheffield editions listed GNSS-denied navigation tracks.
key_takeaways: Navigation tracks recur; winners skew toward working demos with real data

title: El Segundo Defense Tech Hackathon (Feb 2024) - origin of Theseus GPS-denied drone
summary: Aviation Week story (March 2024) on three non-defense engineers who built a GPS-denied drone for under USD 500 at a 24-hour defense tech hackathon; the team became Theseus.
key_takeaways: Cheap visual nav prototypes are a known hackathon genre in the US
